title: Cup product with closed supports
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $n\geq1$ and $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme. Work on the small pro-etale sites with constant coefficient ring sheaves $A_T$ and ambient module derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], put $V=Z\times_XW$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and write $h:V\hookrightarrow X$ for the scheme-theoretic intersection. On affine charts its defining ideal is the sum of the two defining ideals, since $(R/I)\otimes_R(R/J)=R/(I+J)$; in particular $h$ is closed. Direct images below are the underived pro-etale module direct images of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], placed in degree zero.

Let $F,G\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $a,b\in\mathbf Z$. Here $D^+$ means cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. For classes $\alpha\in H_Z^a(X,F)$ and $\beta\in H_W^b(X,G)$, use the pro-etale derived supported sections of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The natural identification of [lem-pur-supported-hom] represents them by morphisms
$$
 \alpha:i_*A_Z\longrightarrow F[a],\qquad
 \beta:j_*A_W\longrightarrow G[b]
$$
in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The tensor product is [def-weil-derived-tensor], with the cochain shifts of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a possibly unbounded complex $K$, the notation for the output of this construction is
$$
 H_V^r(X,K):=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)}(h_*A_V,K[r]).
$$
When $K$ is bounded below, this agrees naturally with the pro-etale supported groups by [lem-pur-supported-hom]. This convention is needed because $F\otimes_A^LG$ need not be bounded below; no finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed on the two inputs.

Here is the specified coefficient isomorphism. On each object $T\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, restrict a section of $A_Z$ on $Z_T=Z\times_XT$ and a section of $A_W$ on $W_T=W\times_XT$ to $V_T=V\times_XT$, and multiply them. These base changes are closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Restrictions commute with this operation, and it is balanced over $A_X(T)$ with the direct-image module actions. The sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] therefore gives the particular map
$$
 \mu:i_*A_Z\otimes_{A_X}j_*A_W\longrightarrow h_*A_V.
$$

The following elementary coefficient calculation verifies its invertibility and flatness entirely on these pro-etale sites. First, $A_T(S)$ is canonically the ring of Zariski-locally constant functions $|S|\to A$, with pointwise operations. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen] identify these functions with morphisms over $T$ into $\coprod_{a\in A}T$. The latter presheaf is a sheaf for pro-etale coverings by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], since these coverings are fpqc by the site definition. Every such function is constant on its open fibres, a Zariski covering, so this sheaf is the sheafification of the constant presheaf: maps from the constant presheaf extend by gluing on those fibres, uniquely. Addition and multiplication agree with their constant-presheaf operations on that cover and hence globally. This also identifies all restriction and scalar maps with restrictions of functions; it does not assert conservativity of geometric stalks on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

For any closed immersion $c:D\hookrightarrow X$ among $i,j,h$, let $J_D\subset A_X$ be the kernel ideal sheaf of restriction $q_D:A_X\to c_*A_D$. Thus $J_D(T)$ consists of locally constant functions on $|T|$ vanishing on $|D_T|$. The restriction $q_D$ is locally surjective: given a locally constant $s$ on the closed subset $|D_T|$, for each point $x\in|D_T|$ choose an open neighbourhood $O_x\subset|T|$ with $s$ constant on $O_x\cap|D_T|$ and extend by that constant; add $T\setminus D_T$ to this open covering and extend there by zero. Consequently
$$
 c_*A_D=A_X/J_D.
$$
Here quotients are sheaf quotients: kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Local surjectivity detects epimorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] and the exact forgetful functor [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful].

For every finite list $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in J_D(T)$ the union of the clopen sets $\{t_l\ne0\}$ is clopen and disjoint from $D_T$. Its characteristic function $e$ belongs to $J_D(T)$, satisfies $e^2=e$, and $et_l=t_l$ for every $l$. For any module sheaf $M$ the mutually inverse tensor formulas
$$
 M\otimes_{A_X}(A_X/J_D)\cong M/J_DM,
 \qquad m\otimes\overline a\longmapsto\overline{am},
 \qquad \overline m\longmapsto m\otimes\overline1
$$
follow from the balanced tensor relations and local lifts of sections of the quotient; $J_DM$ is the sheaf submodule locally consisting of finite sums $\sum t_lm_l$. They glue by the local description of sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], applicable to underlying modules by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets]. If $M\hookrightarrow N$ is a monomorphism and $m\in M(T)$ maps to zero in $N/J_DN$, locally $m=\sum t_ln_l$ in $N$. Choose $e$ as above; then $(1-e)m=0$ in $N$, hence in $M$, so $m=em\in J_DM$. Thus $M/J_DM\to N/J_DN$ is monic. Quotient tensor also preserves right exact sequences: for an epimorphism $N\to P$ lift sections locally, and if the image of $n$ in $P$ is $\sum t_lp_l$, lift the finite list $p_l$ locally to $n_l$; then $n-\sum t_ln_l$ lies in the kernel. This proves exactness of tensor with $c_*A_D$, namely flatness in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

Moreover $J_V=J_Z+J_W$ as sheaf ideals. One inclusion is restriction. For the other, a section $t\in J_V(T)$ has clopen nonzero locus $C$ disjoint from $Z_T\cap W_T$. The three opens $T\setminus Z_T$, $T\setminus W_T$, and $T\setminus C$ cover $T$; there $t$ lies respectively in $J_Z$, in $J_W$, and is zero. Thus it lies locally in the sum. The balanced tensor relations consequently give
$$
 (A_X/J_Z)\otimes_{A_X}(A_X/J_W)
 \cong A_X/(J_Z+J_W)=A_X/J_V,
 \qquad \overline a\otimes\overline b\longmapsto\overline{ab},
$$
with inverse $\overline c\mapsto\overline c\otimes\overline1$. These formulas show that this is exactly $\mu$, not an unspecified isomorphism.

A flat module placed in degree zero is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]: exact tensor preserves the kernels and images computing cohomology, so it carries every acyclic complex to an acyclic complex. Therefore the degree-zero coefficient sheaves are their own K-flat resolutions. The K-flat tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] yields the canonical isomorphism induced by the specified $\mu$,
$$
 \theta:i_*A_Z\otimes_A^Lj_*A_W\xrightarrow{\sim}h_*A_V.
$$
Tensoring morphisms uses [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial]. Fix the shift comparison $\sigma_{a,b}:F[a]\otimes_A^LG[b]\xrightarrow{\sim}(F\otimes_A^LG)[a+b]$ by the ordinary total-complex comparison on K-flat representatives $P,Q$: on a summand $P[a]^r\otimes Q[b]^s$, it sends $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{br}x\otimes y$ in $(P\otimes Q)[a+b]^{r+s}$. With the total differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^r1\otimes d_Q$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the first differential changes this sign by $(-1)^b$ and the second leaves it unchanged; these are exactly the shifted differential signs. Its inverse has the same signs, and it is natural in $P,Q$, so it descends to the indicated derived comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent].

The supported cup product is, by definition, the following composite, read in $H_{Z\cap W}^{a+b}(X,F\otimes_A^LG)$, where $Z\cap W$ means the closed support $V$:
$$
 h_*A_V\xrightarrow{\theta^{-1}}
 i_*A_Z\otimes_A^Lj_*A_W
 \xrightarrow{\alpha\otimes_A^L\beta}F[a]\otimes_A^LG[b]
 \xrightarrow{\sigma_{a,b}}(F\otimes_A^LG)[a+b].
$$

proof.text: Identify the specified constant restriction with the lax monoidal unit of the fixed-scalar lowerStar, conjugated by cupConstantIso. The unit laws give compatibility with composition and coefficient multiplication.

Transport the supported-constant cokernel presentation through sfIntrinsicModuleEquivalence. Its quotient restriction is epic, so each cupCoefficientRestriction is epic. Tensor preserves these epimorphisms. Restrict both supports to their intersection, multiply there via the lax comparison, verify the normalization, and cancel the epic tensor of restriction maps for uniqueness.

For cupCoefficientMap_isIso, use the existing etale closedConstantTensor theorem. Its specified tensor arrow is normalized by the lax direct-image units, using the proved constant-module transition and lowerStar composition laws. The comparison functor is strong monoidal, and its base-change mate is monoidal. At the tensor unit cupConstantIso is its oplax unit, by uniqueness of left adjoints. Hence the three base-change isomorphisms transport the etale tensor isomorphism to an arrow with exactly the defining restriction/multiplication normalization of cupCoefficientMap. The already proved uniqueness identifies these arrows. This replaces the separate balanced quotient/ideal-sum calculation.

For cupCoefficient_flat use openClosedFlatness_etale on the tensor unit and the actual open complement. Apply flat_comparisonUpperStar_obj and transport along the proved underived isIso_lowerStarComparisonUpperStarBaseChange, valid for closed immersions because they are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. No quasi-compactness of the open complement is needed.

For the derived theorem, a flat sheaf in degree zero is K-flat. Apply the source-library isIso_mu_Qh_of_kFlat to that complex and the other degree-zero complex, transport through the homotopy quotient comparison, and compose with the single-complex tensor isomorphism and the ordinary coefficient isomorphism just proved. Package the derived monoidal structure together with the localization lax structure, and transport from the canonical pair by equality, avoiding expansion of their data.

proof_origin.place: All four coefficient obligations: normalized restriction and supported-constant presentation; etale tensor isomorphism transported through strong monoidal comparison and its base-change mate; etale open-closed flatness; degree-zero K-flat localization tensor comparison. All four Lean proofs are complete from the stated declarations.

split_report.summary: Re-split after E4/C4: restored the finite coefficient datum A=A_{E,n} and pro-etale sites fixed by the current convention unit, citing lem-pur-supported-hom directly for both inputs. Reconstructed mu by restriction and multiplication on pro-etale test objects. Verified its exact coefficient quotient model, flatness by local idempotents, and intersection tensor using existing generic nodes and explicit elementary calculations. Removed every etale-only support, geometric-stalk, and K-flat criterion dependency, including the remark-only lem-amb-closed-support-hom. Retained the explicit unbounded Hom output and supplied a signed total-complex shift map. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves; existing search and report history preserved.
split_report.blueprint: Current main-20261015 definition: supported-Hom input representation, intersection coefficient identification, tensor of morphisms, and sum of shifts. Companion proof: coefficient tensor is underived and flat. Its stalk shorthand is replaced by the explicit sheaf quotient/idempotent calculation on pro-etale test objects. Convention unit sk-def-purity-conv fixes Lambda=A=A_{E,n} and the pro-etale sites.

tool_uses.why: Fpqc descent makes the locally constant-function coefficient model a sheaf for the actual pro-etale coverings; the unit supplies no such general descent tool.
Existence of the constant scheme whose relative morphisms model locally constant coefficient functions; a generic scheme construction, not a substitute Kummer route.
Identifies the specific relative morphisms into the constant scheme with clopen decompositions, on arbitrary test schemes; no pro-etale stalk assertion is substituted.
Keeps each test-object support closed, permitting the explicit local extension argument; a generic geometric tool.
Detects the displayed quotient epimorphisms and gives local lifts in the flatness argument on this site.
Transfers the general-site local epimorphism criterion to module sheaves via its exact forgetful functor.
Gives local representatives and local equality for the sheaf quotients and tensor relations; generic sheafification tool.
Allows the stated set-level local sheafification criterion for module quotients by forgetting their abelian structure.
Generic ringed-site K-flat comparison and two-variable localization justify the coefficient tensor and explicit shift comparison.
Supplies tensor on the pair of supported derived morphisms, in precisely the pro-etale category used here.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$ be
closed immersions, and
write $h:Z\times_XW\hookrightarrow X$. For classes
$\alpha\in H_Z^a(X,F)$ and $\beta\in H_W^b(X,G)$ in
supported cohomology, represent
them by morphisms as in [lem-pur-supported-hom].
Their *supported cup product* is the morphism

$$
h_*\Lambda_{Z\times_XW}
\cong i_*\Lambda_Z\otimes^L_\Lambda j_*\Lambda_W
\xrightarrow{\alpha\otimes\beta}(F\otimes^L_\Lambda G)[a+b],
$$

read as an element of $H_{Z\cap W}^{a+b}(X,F\otimes^L_\Lambda G)$.
The first identification is the stalkwise identification of the
coefficient sheaves. Tensor and shifts are those
of derived tensor.

proof.text:
The first identification is well defined: each stalk of the coefficient
sheaves is either $0$ or the free module $\Lambda$, so these sheaves are flat
and their tensor is the coefficient sheaf on the intersection.
